classification.difficultyReason: Use the deck’s ranks and suits to determine each restricted set and count the queens within it.

content.prompt: A card is selected at random from a standard deck of 52 cards. Find the probability that the card is

children.label: a
children.prompt: a queen given that the card is a picture card?

answer.worked:
Each of the four suits has three picture cards (jack, queen and king), so there are $12$ picture cards and $4$ of them are queens.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{queen}\mid\text{picture card})&=\frac{4}{12}\\P(\text{queen}\mid\text{picture card})&=\frac{1}{3}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: a queen given that the card selected is red?

answer.worked:
Hearts and diamonds give $26$ red cards. Each of those suits has one queen.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{queen}\mid\text{red})&=\frac{2}{26}\\P(\text{queen}\mid\text{red})&=\frac{1}{13}\end{align*}$$
